stories.title: Wall Street's rally shows cracks beneath the surface
stories.summary: MarketWatch reports that the broader stock market rally looks weaker on closer inspection. Headline index gains mask softer signals underneath, such as narrower participation across stocks. The report urges investors to look past the top-line numbers.
stories.whyItMatters: A rally driven by only a few stocks can reverse quickly if those leaders stumble.
whatToWatch: Whether more stocks join the rally, not just index leaders
Any pullback in the stocks driving the gains
questions: Which stocks or sectors are propping up the headline index moves?
What would trigger a broader market pullback?

stories.title: Upcoming jobs report could push 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields sharply higher
stories.summary: MarketWatch reports that the next jobs report could send long-term Treasury yields surging. Bond investors are watching the data closely for signs of labor market strength. A stronger-than-expected report could push yields higher still.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher long-term yields raise borrowing costs across the economy, including mortgages and corporate debt.
whatToWatch: The next jobs report release date
The reaction in 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields
questions: How strong would the jobs data need to be to trigger a sharp yield move?

stories.title: Rising bond yields raise risk for debt-heavy AI companies
stories.summary: CNBC reports that AI companies carrying large debt loads face increased risk as bond yields spike. Higher yields raise the cost of servicing that debt. This adds financial pressure on firms that have borrowed heavily to fund AI buildouts.
stories.whyItMatters: Much of the AI infrastructure spending boom depends on cheap financing, so higher yields could slow it down.
whatToWatch: Bond yield levels in coming weeks
Refinancing moves by heavily indebted AI companies
questions: Which AI companies carry the most debt exposure?

stories.title: NFL stadiums deploy drone defense tech this season
stories.summary: CNBC reports NFL stadiums are using drone defense technology this season. The aim is to reduce disruptions from unauthorized drones during games. The move responds to growing concern about drone intrusions at large events.
stories.whyItMatters: Drone-security spending points to a growing market for counter-drone technology at stadiums and other public events.
whatToWatch: Whether the technology reduces drone incidents this season

stories.title: Institutional money retakes the driver's seat in the stock market
stories.summary: CNBC reports that Wall Street institutional money is again driving the stock market, taking over from the small individual investors who had been a bigger force. This marks a shift in who is moving prices day to day.
stories.whyItMatters: When institutions dominate trading, price moves can reflect large concentrated bets rather than broad retail sentiment.
whatToWatch: Further shifts in trading volume between institutional and retail investors
questions: What caused retail investors to pull back?

stories.whyItMatters: Storm-driven flight disruptions hit airline operations and revenue, and fee waivers are an early sign of the scale expected.

stories.title: Iran's foreign minister keeps talks with U.S. open as navy claims drone capture
stories.summary: CNBC reports that Iran's foreign minister is keeping indirect talks with the United States open. Separately, Iran's navy claims it captured an underwater drone. Both developments come amid ongoing tension between the two countries.
stories.whyItMatters: Iran-U.S. tensions affect oil prices and regional risk premiums that ripple into energy and broader markets.

Any details on Iran's claimed drone capture
questions: What terms are under discussion in the indirect talks?
